question.:question/problem:
$$
X+Y=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\,Z=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Consider the matrices above. Knowing that the matrix representation $T=\begin{bmatrix}{t}_{11} & {t}_{12} \\ {t}_{21} & {t}_{22}\end{bmatrix}$ of a linear transformation $T$ is given by

$$
T=XZ+YZ,
$$

find the values ${t}_{ij}.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${t}_{11}=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
$\,{t}_{12}=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-2}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                                

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${t}_{21}=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-3}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
$\,{t}_{22}=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-4}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
We apply the distributive law

$$
XZ+YZ=(X+Y)Z.
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =XZ+YZ \\  & =(X+Y)Z \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can apply the distributive law

$$
BA+BC=B(A+C).
$$

So, we calculate $A+C$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+C & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & -1 \\ 4 & -2 & 3 \\ -5 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 3 & 1 \\ -4 & 2 & -3 \\ 5 & -1 & -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}BA+BC & =B(A+C) \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}8 & \sqrt{3} & \sqrt{7} \\ \sqrt{5} & \sqrt{6} & \sqrt{2} \\ \sqrt{7} & \sqrt{2} & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We apply the distributive law 

$$
AB+AC=A(B+C).
$$

So, we calculate $B+C$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}B+C & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -3 & 5\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ -4 & 3 & -4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & ={I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB+AC & =A(B+C) \\  & =A{I}_{3} \\  & =A \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 5\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can apply the distributive law

$$
AC+BC=(A+B)C.
$$

So, we calculate $A+B$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+B & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & -1 & -4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & ={I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AC+BC & =(A+B)C \\  & ={I}_{3}\cdot C \\  & =C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 4 & 2 \\ 5 & -1 & 3\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We apply the distributive law

$$
AB+CB=(A+C)B.
$$

So, we calculate $A+C$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+C & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -5 & -1 \\ -9 & 10 & 11\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-5 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 \\ 9 & -10 & -13\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =-2{I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB+CB & =(A+C)B \\  & =-2{I}_{3}B \\  & =-2B \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-2\sqrt{2} & -2 & -2\sqrt{3} \\ -2 & -2\sqrt{5} & -2 \\ -2\sqrt{7} & -2 & -2\sqrt{2}\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We apply the distributive law

$$
AC+BC=(A+B)C.
$$

So, we calculate $A+B$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+B & =\begin{bmatrix}7 & 6 & -1 \\ 3 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-3 & -6 & 1 \\ -3 & 8 & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =4{I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AC+BC & =(A+B)C \\  & =4{I}_{3}C \\  & =4C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}8\sqrt{5} & -4 & 12 \\ 0 & 4\sqrt{3} & 16 \\ -8 & 12 & 20\text{ }\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can apply the distributive law

$$
AC+BC=(A+B)C.
$$

So, we calculate $A+B$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+B & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 5 \\ 4 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 3 & -4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AC+BC & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & \sqrt{6} \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -6 & 3\sqrt{6}\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can apply the distributive law

$$
AB+AC=A(B+C).
$$

So, we calculate $B+C$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}B+C & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2 & \sqrt{3}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 & \sqrt{3} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB+AC & =A(B+C) \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & \sqrt{3} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & \sqrt{3} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We apply the distributive law

$$
CB-CA=C(B-A).
$$

So, compute $B-A$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}B-A & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -5\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =-3{I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}CB-CA & =C(B-A) \\  & =C(-3{I}_{3}) \\  & =-3C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 & 0 \\ -6 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We apply the distributive law on the right:

$$
AC-BC=(A-B)C.
$$

So, compute $A-B$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A-B & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & 0\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}-2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & -4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =4{I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AC-BC & =(A-B)C \\  & =(4{I}_{3})C \\  & =4C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We apply the distributive law 

$$
CB+CA=C(B+A).
$$

So, we calculate $B+A$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}B+A & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & -\sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -\sqrt{3} & -2 & 5\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & \sqrt{2} \\ -1 & 3 & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 2 & -1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =4{I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}CB+CA & =C(B+A) \\  & =C\cdot 4{I}_{3} \\  & =4C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can apply the distributive law

$$
AC+BC=(A+B)C.
$$

So, we calculate $A+B$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+B & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 & -3 \\ -3 & -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & -2 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AC+BC & =(A+B)C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\begin{bmatrix}-2 & \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ 1 & -\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ -2 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We apply the distributive law

$$
AB+CB=(A+C)B.
$$

So, we calculate $A+C$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+C & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & 1 \\ -2 & -2 & 3 \\ -8 & 9 & 9\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 7 & -3 \\ 8 & -9 & -4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{bmatrix} \\  & =5{I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB+CB & =(A+C)B \\  & =5{I}_{3}B \\  & =5B \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}40 & 5 & 5\sqrt{3} \\ 15 & 25 & 5 \\ -10\sqrt{7} & 5 & 15\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We apply the distributive law

$$
AC+BC=(A+B)C.
$$

So, we calculate $A+B$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+B & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & -6\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 & -2 & 1 \\ -3 & 6 & -1 \\ -3 & -2 & 9\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =3{I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AC+BC & =(A+B)C \\  & =3{I}_{3}C \\  & =3C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 3\sqrt{2} & 3\sqrt{3} \\ 6 & 3\sqrt{3} & 6 \\ 9 & 6 & 3\sqrt{5}\text{ }\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$
